p: those days came: Not when Joseph went to dwell at Nazareth, but a great while after, about fifteen years: for in the 30th year of his life Jesus was baptized by John: therefore "those days" means the time when Jesus remained as an inhabitant of the town of Nazareth.

John the Baptist: John, who through his singular holiness and rare austerity of life caused men to cast their eyes on him, prepares the way for Christ who is following fast on his heels, as the prophet Isaiah foretold, and delivers the sum of the gospel, which a short time later would be delivered more fully.

wilderness of Judaea: In a hilly country, which was nonetheless inhabited, for Zacharias dwelt there, Lu 1:39,40, and there was Joab's house, 1Ki 2:34; and besides these, Joshua makes mention of six towns that were in the wilderness, Jos 15:61,62.
Repent ye: The word in the greek signifies a changing of our minds and heart from evil to better.
kingdom of heaven is at hand: The kingdom of Messiah, whose government will be heavenly, and nothing but heavenly.
make his paths straight: Make him a plain and smooth way.
locusts and wild honey: Locusts were a type of meat which certain of the eastern people use, who were therefore called devourers of locusts.
Jerusalem: The people of Jerusalem.
confessing their sins: Acknowledging that they were saved only by free remission and forgiveness of their sins.
But when he saw many of: There is nothing that shuts up the way of mercy and salvation from us so much as the opinion of our own righteousness does.
Bring forth therefore fruits meet for: True repentance is an inward thing which has its seat in the mind and heart.

And: The faith of the fathers does not benefit you unbelieving children at all: and yet for all that, God does not play the liar, nor deal unfaithfully in his covenant which he made with the holy fathers.
think not to say: Think not that you have any reason to be proud of Abraham.
within yourselves: In your hearts.

I indeed baptize you with water: We may neither dwell upon the signs which God has ordained as means to lead us into our salvation, neither upon those that minister them: but we must climb up to the matter itself, that is to say, to Christ, who inwardly works that effectually, which is outwardly signified to us.

repentance: The outward sign reminds us of this, that we must change our lives and become better, assuring us as by a seal, that we are ingrafted into Christ; by which our old man dies and the new man rises up; Ro 6:4.
Whose fan is in his hand: The triumphs of the wicked will end in everlasting torment.
purge his floor: Will clean it thoroughly, and make a full riddance.
Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to: Christ sanctified our baptism in himself.
all righteousness: All such things as it has appointed for us to keep.
him: To John.
And lo a voice from heaven: Christ's full consecration and authorization to the office of mediator is shown by the Father's own voice and a visible sign of the Holy Spirit.

well pleased: The Greek word signifies a thing of great worth and such as highly pleases a man. So then the Father says that Christ is the only man whom when he beholds, looking at what opinion he had conceived of us, he lays it clean aside.
